git.title: Git behavior
git.intro: Defaults for all repositories in this profile. A repository can set its own pull mode and auto-fetch.

autoFetch.title: Auto-fetch
autoFetch.description: Regularly fetches all remotes of the open repositories in the background – without asking, using saved credentials. 0 turns it off; per repository it can be turned off in its settings.

autoPrune.title: Prune stale remote branches
autoPrune.description: On fetch, removes local references to branches that no longer exist on the remote.

pushAfterCommit.title: Push after commit
pushAfterCommit.description: The “Push afterwards” checkbox in the commit panel is then checked by default.

squashOnMerge.title: Squash on merge
squashOnMerge.description: When merging, combines all commits of the branch into a single change instead of creating a merge commit.

deleteOrigFiles.title: Delete .orig files after resolving a conflict
deleteOrigFiles.description: Removes the backup copies that merge tools leave next to a conflicted file.

defaultBranch.title: Default branch name
defaultBranch.description: The name of the first branch in repositories you create here.

initialCommits.title: Commits on first load
initialCommits.description: How many commits the graph shows right after opening (at least 500). More takes longer to start.

lazyLoad.title: Load more while scrolling
lazyLoad.description: Loads older commits as soon as you reach the end of the graph.

rememberTabs.title: Remember tabs
rememberTabs.description: Reopens the last tabs of this profile on startup and when switching to it.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.intro: How the interface looks, the same in all profiles. Everything here takes effect immediately.

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: “System” follows the light or dark setting of your operating system.

language.title: Language / Sprache
language.description: Language of the interface. “System” follows the language of your operating system. Changing it reloads the window.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Enlarges or shrinks the whole interface (80 to 200 %). Also works with {{mod}} and plus or minus. In a small window, only as much zoom applies as fits – make the window larger for more.

dateFormat.title: Date format
dateFormat.description: How times appear in the graph and in the commit details. Example: {{example}}

toolbarLabels.title: Toolbar labels
toolbarLabels.description: Shows what each toolbar icon does below it.

showInitials.title: Initials instead of avatars
showInitials.description: Shows authors as colored initials instead of loading their avatars from GitHub (looked up by commit email address).

diff.title: Diff and editor
diff.intro: How changes and files are displayed, the same in all profiles.

mode.title: Diff view
mode.description: A diff opens in this view. You can switch at any time in the diff itself.

wordWrap.title: Word wrap
wordWrap.description: Wraps long lines instead of scrolling them horizontally.

ignoreWhitespace.title: Ignore whitespace
ignoreWhitespace.description: Hides changes that only affect spaces, tabs or line endings.

fontSize.title: Font size
fontSize.description: Applies to the diff, editor and conflict tool (8 to 40 pixels).

tabSize.title: Tab width
tabSize.description: How many columns a tab takes up (1 to 16).

external.title: External programs
external.intro: Command lines for “Open in …”. {path} stands for the file or folder, {repo} for the repository. An empty field uses your system's default, or your Git configuration for the diff and merge tool.

editor.title: Editor
editor.description: Opens a file or the whole repository in your editor.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.description: Opens a terminal in the repository folder; {path} is the folder here.

diffTool.title: Diff tool
diffTool.description: Shows the diff of a file in a separate program (“Open in external diff tool” in the diff and the file menu). {local} is the old version, {remote} the new one; if both are missing, the app appends them. Empty: git difftool with the tool from your Git configuration.
diffTool.placeholder: git difftool (diff.tool from your Git configuration)

mergeTool.title: Merge tool
mergeTool.description: Opens a conflicted file in a separate program instead of the built-in conflict tool. {base} is the common ancestor, {local} your version, {remote} the incoming one, {merged} the file the result goes into; without placeholders the program only gets {merged}. Empty: git mergetool with the tool from your Git configuration.
mergeTool.placeholder: git mergetool (merge.tool from your Git configuration)

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: Which messages appear at the bottom right without you having started anything.

onFetch.title: On fetch results
onFetch.description: Notifies you when an auto-fetch has found new commits or branches.

onError.title: On background errors
onError.description: Notifies you when a background task fails unexpectedly. If auto-fetch only lacks the network or a login, it stays quiet and the error goes to the log. You always see errors of your own actions.

profiles.title: Profile and identity
profiles.intro: The name and email address your commits are signed with.

noAuthor.title: No author set
noAuthor.name: The name is missing.
noAuthor.hint: Git cannot create commits without both. Enter them below.

name.title: Profile name
name.description: Only for you, to tell profiles apart – such as “Work” and “Personal”.
name.empty: The profile name must not be empty.

authorName.title: Author name
authorName.description: Appears as the author of every commit you create.

email.title: Email
email.description: Hosts use this address to link commits to your account.

syncGitconfig.title: Write name and email to the global gitconfig
syncGitconfig.description: Sets both as user.name and user.email in your global Git configuration – then they also apply in the terminal and other programs. When off, the file stays as it is and Git uses what is there.

profiles.listIntro: Each profile has its own identity, tabs and settings.
profiles.lastBlocked: The last profile cannot be deleted.
profiles.activeBlocked: The active profile cannot be deleted. Switch to another one first.

delete.title: Delete profile “{{name}}”?
delete.body: Its settings, its tab list, the added SSH keys and the saved credentials are removed. Repositories and key files on disk stay where they are. This cannot be undone.
delete.label: Delete profile {{name}}

create.doneHint: Use “Switch” in the list to make it the active profile.
create.title: New profile
create.description: A second identity with its own tabs and settings, for example for work.

about.title: About
about.intro: What is running here and where it stores its data – useful for bug reports.
about.tagline: Desktop Git client. Works locally, without an account with us and without telemetry.
about.dataDirHint: The data directory holds settings, profiles, tab lists and the log. Your repositories are not stored there. Tokens, passwords and API keys are not stored there either, but in the operating system's keychain.
about.privacyGit: Git connections to the remotes of your repositories: clone, fetch, pull, push, submodules and LFS. This includes auto-fetch – by default every minute for every open repository, without asking and using saved credentials. To turn it off: Git behavior › Auto-fetch to 0, or per repository.
about.privacyHosts: Requests to GitHub or GitLab if you have connected an account there – only for pull requests and issues, with your own token.
about.privacyLinks: Links from READMEs, pull requests and issues are opened by the system browser, and only after asking.
about.privacyRest: Nothing else: no telemetry, no update checks, no images or fonts from the internet. Forkyard only runs commands a repository brings along after you have agreed.
about.privacyAvatars: Avatars of commit authors from GitHub (avatars.githubusercontent.com): the commit email address is sent to look up the account; results are kept for a week. Turn off: Appearance › Initials instead of avatars.

project.intro: Applies only to {{repo}} and takes precedence over the profile.

identity.title: Identity and access
identity.authorName: Name for commits in this repository; stored in its .git/config.
identity.authorEmail: Email address for commits in this repository; stored in its .git/config.
identity.sshKey: Only applies to fetch, pull and push from the app, even if the profile uses the SSH agent. A core.sshCommand of this repository stays the basis; the key is appended.
identity.agentFallback: SSH agent or your SSH configuration
identity.noKeys: No SSH key has been added to the profile yet.
identity.accountDescription: For pull requests, issues and avatars. The profile has one account per host; it applies to all repositories there.

git.title: Pull and fetch
git.pullModeDescription: How the pull button works in this repository.
git.autoFetchOffInProfile: Auto-fetch is off in the profile (interval 0 under “Git behavior”); here it can only be turned off additionally.
git.autoFetchDescription: When off, the app only fetches the remotes here when you click fetch or pull yourself – good for very large repositories.

files.title: Files and hooks
files.encodingDescription: The app reads and writes text files that are not recognizable as UTF-8 in this encoding.
files.hooksDescription: Folder with the Git hooks of this repository (core.hooksPath), relative to the repository or absolute. Empty = .git/hooks.
files.templateDescription: Text file whose content appears as a draft in every new commit message (commit.template). Empty = no template.

links.title: Ticket links
links.host: Link issue numbers to the host
links.hostDescription: #123 opens the issue or pull request on the repository's host; on GitLab, !123 opens the merge request.
links.noHost: No remote of this repository is on GitHub, GitLab or a connected instance – there is nothing to link to.
links.keysHint: Optional, separated by commas: only these keys are linked (e.g. ABC for ABC-123). Empty = every key of the form ABC-123.
links.redmineHint: Redmine links #123 to its issues; if the host links are on as well, your tracker wins.
links.patternHint: Regular expression (ASCII): groups (…) and (?:…), \d \w \s \b; no lookarounds or back-references, at most 200 characters.
links.urlHint: Starts with http:// or https:// and a fixed host; $0 is the whole match, $1 … the groups.
links.testPlaceholder: A commit message, e.g. Fixes OPS-42
links.testInvalid: The pattern is not a valid regular expression.
links.testNested: A repeated group must not contain a repetition itself, e.g. (a+)+.
links.fileFromWorktree: Read from the working directory. These rules come with the repository and can only be changed in the file.
links.fileFromHead: Read from the last commit (HEAD); the working directory has no such file.
links.fileError: The rules could not be loaded.

forget.body: The passwords, tokens and passphrases of this profile are deleted from the system keychain. The app will ask for them again on the next fetch, pull or push.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.intro: What the app has saved for remotes. The secrets themselves are stored in your system keychain and are never shown here.

noKeyring.title: No keychain available
noKeyring.body: So the app cannot save anything and asks again for every connection. On Linux, a running Secret Service (GNOME Keyring or KWallet) is usually missing. A Git credential helper or an SSH agent still work.

empty.title: Nothing saved
empty.body: When a remote asks for a password, token or passphrase, you can check “Save in the system keychain” in the dialog. The entry then appears here.

ssh.noPublicKeyHint: The file {{path}} is missing or empty.
ssh.copiedHint: Paste it at your host under “SSH keys”.
ssh.copyFailedHint: The clipboard is not available. Select the key text and copy it manually.

import.title: Add key
import.label: Label
import.noPub: There is no .pub file next to the private key.

ssh.title: SSH keys
ssh.intro: Keys Git uses to sign in to your remotes over SSH.

useAgent.title: Use the system SSH agent
useAgent.description: When on, your SSH agent and SSH configuration choose the key. When off, the app always uses the default key from this list.

noDefault.title: No default key chosen
noDefault.body: The SSH agent is off, but no key is marked as default. Choose “Use as default” below.

empty.title: No key yet
empty.intro: You need one for remotes with an SSH address (git@…). In three steps:
empty.step1: Generate – “Generate key” creates a new pair in the SSH folder.
empty.step2: Copy – “Copy public key” puts it on the clipboard.
empty.step3: Add – paste it at your host in the account settings under “SSH keys”.

makeDefault.doneAgent: It is used as soon as you turn off “Use the system SSH agent”.

remove.title: Remove key “{{label}}”?
remove.body: Only the entry in this list disappears. The files stay where they are:
remove.done: Entry “{{label}}” removed – the files are still there

ssh.fileMissingHint: At least one of the two key files is gone.

dialog.labelMissing: Give the key a label, e.g. “Work laptop”.
dialog.fileEmpty: The file name must not be empty.
dialog.fileChars: Only a file name, not a path – without \ / : * ? " < > |.
dialog.filePub: Without “.pub” – that is the name of the public key file.
dialog.passphraseShort: At least 5 characters – or leave it empty.
dialog.repeatMismatch: The two entries do not match.
dialog.doneHint: Now copy the public key and add it at your host.
dialog.fileExists: A file with this name already exists in the SSH folder. Choose another one – nothing is overwritten.
dialog.failed: The key could not be generated.
dialog.title: Generate SSH key
dialog.description: Creates a new key pair (ed25519) in your SSH folder. Existing files are never overwritten.
dialog.label: Label
dialog.labelHint: Shown in this list. The public key ends with the email of your profile – without an email, the label.
dialog.fileNameHint: The public key gets the same name with “.pub”.
dialog.passphraseHint: Protects the file in case someone copies it. Empty = none.
